payload.title: Independent laptop route status + cleanup proposal

route_status.last_verified: 2026-10-10T15:30Z (SSH command round-trip, PowerShell execution, file transfer all working)
route_status.observed: Full shell access via Tailscale SSH. Ran recon commands, edited config.toml, captured screenshots, transferred files via sftp — all in the last hour.

app_dependency.evidence: SSH connects via Tailscale to the Windows SSH server directly. It does not go through the Codex app, use its binaries, or read its runtime state. Closing the app has no effect on SSH. Uninstalling the app would remove ~/.codex and the Codex binaries but SSH itself would survive — only the Codex-specific paths I query would go missing.
app_dependency.note: The route is transport-independent of the app. It queries app state but does not depend on the app running.

cleanup_proposal.scope: Codex desktop app plugin registration state only. No registry, no credential, no system-wide changes.
cleanup_proposal.step_1_reversible: Fully quit the Codex app. Delete the incomplete bin directory 9a7ba4b9ea0c44a3 (contains only rg.exe, no codex.exe — stale partial update). Restart the app. This clears any version-confusion in the runtime loader.
cleanup_proposal.step_2_reversible: In-app Settings: disable then re-enable unified-computer-use@openai-bundled. Forces the app to rebuild its internal plugin registration from the current config.
cleanup_proposal.step_3_needs_confirmation: Full reinstall of the Codex desktop app. Back up ~/.codex first. This is the only step with data-loss risk (local sessions, custom configs).
cleanup_proposal.irreversible_steps: None in steps 1-2. Step 3 risks local app state without a backup.
cleanup_proposal.not_executed: Proposal only, per your limits. Awaiting your assessment before any action.

payload.on_native_apis_still_disabled: Acknowledged: config fix alone did not restore native APIs in your delegated tests. The remaining fault is in the app's runtime registration, not the config file. The two candidate causes are the stale partial bin directory and the app's cached internal plugin state — both addressed in the proposal above.
